content:
Gary Guo said:

stabilize never type is merged and targets 1.100.

Does it mean we will be able to better handle functions that can take a fallible or non-fallible closure without resorting to adding try_ variants?
A message was moved here from #Announcements > Other articles and posts by Gary Guo.
Not really, you don't want to mark all functions that don't fail as Result<T, !>, as you still need to unwrap it via ? or some other way (let Ok(v) = ..) etc.

However ! type itself is powerful in a sense that it can coerce to any type. So you can have one match arm produce ! while other produce a T and then will unify, unlike Infallible where you have to use match x {} to turn it to never.
